96243.title: Who Keeps the Record
96243.excerpt: Roy Batty spends his last minute on an inventory nobody else can carry. Qoheleth ran the same audit over vineyards and houses and called the whole of it hevel. The disagreement between them is not about whether the moments mattered. It is about whether anybody is keeping the record.

94219.title: Why Did Paul Tell Women to Cover Their Heads? (11 of 12)
94219.excerpt: The passage argues from nature and then seems to contradict itself. One striking proposal about a single Greek word, and what is worth keeping from it.

94213.title: Beelzebul and Who Counts as Family (5 of 6)
94213.excerpt: His own relatives think he is out of his mind and the scribes think he is possessed. Mark puts the two verdicts in one scene, and the answer redefines family.

94211.title: The Paralytic and the Authority to Forgive (3 of 6)
94211.excerpt: Four men dig through a roof, and it was probably Jesus’s own. What he says to the man on the mat starts the argument that ends at the high priest’s house.

94214.title: The Yeast of the Pharisees and of Herod (6 of 6)
94214.excerpt: Two rival visions of the kingdom, both of them diluted, and the disciples think he is talking about sandwiches. What each party wanted God to do for them.

94217.title: What Was Paul’s Thorn in the Flesh? (9 of 12)
94217.excerpt: Everyone assumes an illness. The phrase comes from the Old Testament and there it always means people, and Paul calls it a messenger rather than a condition.

94218.title: Does Paul Forbid Women to Teach or Preach? (10 of 12)
94218.excerpt: One verse set against a great deal of counter-evidence in the same author. What Ephesus was, what the rare Greek verb means, and why the setting matters.

94220.title: Why Does Acts Not Record Paul’s Death? (12 of 12)
94220.excerpt: The book ends with him alive under house arrest, and the silence is itself evidence. What it implies about when Acts was written, and about Luke’s Gospel.

93438.title: The Tree of Knowledge and the Transfer of Dominion
93438.excerpt: The world was good, not perfect. The tree gave something Genesis never names, and I had to throw out my own best guess at it. What survives is a chain: dominion given, lost, claimed, and taken back at the cross.

93441.title: The Tree of Knowledge: What We Actually Know, Sorted by Confidence
93441.excerpt: Every claim I could find about the tree of knowing good and bad, sorted into what the text says, what the Hebrew carries, what is only tradition, what is theory, and what is invented. Including the readings of mine that did not survive.

93480.title: Tertullian, Perpetua, and Origen Explained (5 of 8)
93480.excerpt: The man who gave the West its trinitarian vocabulary and then left the church, a prison diary by a young mother, and the most brilliant scholar of the age.

93495.title: How Did Judas Iscariot Die? And Matthias (13 of 13)
93495.excerpt: Scripture gives two accounts of Judas’s death and does not reconcile them. What each text says, why the difference is real, and how the twelfth seat was filled.

93494.title: Who Was Simon the Zealot? (12 of 13)
93494.excerpt: His title may not mean what the sermons say. What Cananaean meant, when the Zealot party actually formed, and whether Simon had reason to want Matthew dead.

93493.title: Who Was Thaddaeus? Jude, Not Iscariot (11 of 13)
93493.excerpt: One recorded question, two names, and a famous forged correspondence. Who Thaddaeus was, why he probably did not write Jude, and what the Abgar legend hides.

93492.title: Who Was James the Less? The Three Jameses (10 of 13)
93492.excerpt: Four lists, four mentions, no recorded words. Who James son of Alphaeus was, why he is confused with two other men named James, and what that confusion costs.

93491.title: Who Was Matthew the Tax Collector? (9 of 13)
93491.excerpt: Tax farming made extortion structural rather than incidental. How Matthew made his money, why that made him a traitor, and where the synagogue-ban claim rests.

93490.title: Did Thomas the Apostle Go to India? (8 of 13)
93490.excerpt: The nickname is modern and the early church read him the opposite way. What Scripture says, when he got shrunk, and the evidence for the India mission.

93489.title: Was Bartholomew the Same as Nathanael? (7 of 13)
93489.excerpt: The Synoptics name Bartholomew and never Nathanael. John does the reverse. Why the two are traditionally identified, and why that remains an inference.

93488.title: Who Was the Apostle Philip? Two Philips (6 of 13)
93488.excerpt: Two men named Philip in the New Testament, and the early church mixed them up. What Scripture records, and why most Philip traditions belong to the other one.

93487.title: Who Was the Apostle John? Patmos and Ephesus (5 of 13)
93487.excerpt: The one apostle the earliest tradition says died of old age. What Scripture records about John, the Patmos exile, and the honest state of the authorship debate.

93486.title: How Did James the Apostle Die? Acts 12 (4 of 13)
93486.excerpt: James son of Zebedee is the only apostle whose death Scripture records. What Acts 12 says, why it can be dated, and where the Spain tradition comes from.

93472.title: Who Was the Apostle Andrew? (3 of 13)
93472.excerpt: Andrew brought Peter to Jesus and then left almost no trace. What Scripture records, and why Scotland claimed an apostle who never went within a thousand miles.

93463.title: Who Was the Apostle Peter? Life and Death (2 of 13)
93463.excerpt: Peter is the most documented life among the Twelve, and the only one whose death Scripture predicts without narrating. This walks the call, the confession, the denial, the restoration, the years in Acts, and the point where the evidence for his death runs out and the legend takes over.

93454.title: Who Were the Twelve Apostles of Jesus? (1 of 13)
93454.excerpt: Scripture names the Twelve in four separate lists and narrates exactly one apostolic death. This walks the lists, the meaning of the title, and the honest line where the martyrdom traditions stop being evidence.

93499.title: Who Was James the Brother of Jesus? (4 of 4)
93499.excerpt: He did not believe during the ministry and ended up leading the Jerusalem church. What Scripture records about James, and why he is confused with two apostles.

93498.title: Who Wrote the Book of Jude? (3 of 4)
93498.excerpt: A brother of Jesus who did not believe during the ministry, writing a letter that quotes a book outside the canon. Who Jude was and why his letter was disputed.

93497.title: Who Was Mark in the New Testament? (2 of 4)
93497.excerpt: He quit a mission trip, split Paul and Barnabas over it, and ended up writing a Gospel. What Scripture says about John Mark and what tradition adds to it.

93496.title: Who Was Luke and Did He Write Acts? (1 of 4)
93496.excerpt: He wrote more of the New Testament than anyone except Paul, never met Jesus, and says so in his own opening lines. What is known about Luke and what is guessed.

93504.title: Which New Testament Books Were Disputed? (5 of 6)
93504.excerpt: A stable core of twenty books and a long argument about seven. What Origen and Eusebius each sorted where, and why Revelation got listed in two categories.

93501.title: Did the Early Church Quote the Gospels? (2 of 6)
93501.excerpt: The generation after the apostles used the writings without arguing for them, which is stronger evidence than argument. Who quoted what, book by book.

93500.title: When Was the New Testament Written? (1 of 6)
93500.excerpt: The documents existed and were being circulated before anyone drew up a list. What the letters say about their own reading, and where books cite other books.

93507.title: Clean and Unclean: Why Jesus Was Cryptic (2 of 6)
93507.excerpt: People had been tortured to death for refusing unclean food. Saying what he said plainly would have told a nation its martyrs died in the wrong ditch.

93509.title: When Was Jesus Born? The Date Theories (12 of 12)
93509.excerpt: September, December, or unknowable. The constellation argument, the nine-months-from-death calculation, and the priestly course theory, each weighed honestly.

93563.title: What Is the Ascension of Jesus? (11 of 12)
93563.excerpt: Forty days after the resurrection he was taken up from the Mount of Olives. What the ascension claims, why it is enthronement language, and what it began.

93519.title: The Resurrection Appearances of Jesus (10 of 12)
93519.excerpt: Who saw him, in what order, and over how long. The appearances the Gospels record, the earliest creed listing them, and the detail that resists invention.

93518.title: The Crucifixion of Jesus: What Happened (9 of 12)
93518.excerpt: What the Gospels record about Golgotha, the darkness, the torn veil, and the burial, plus what Roman crucifixion actually involved and why the burial matters.

93517.title: What Happened During Holy Week? Day by Day (8 of 12)
93517.excerpt: A staged royal entry, a cursed fig tree, a day of failed traps, a Passover meal reassigned, and six trials before dawn. The final week laid out in order.

93516.title: Jesus in Judea and Perea: The Final Year (7 of 12)
93516.excerpt: He set his face toward Jerusalem, and the great parables come from this stretch. The Good Samaritan, the Prodigal Son, and the sign that got him killed.

93515.title: Peter’s Confession and the Transfiguration (6 of 12)
93515.excerpt: The hinge the Gospels turn on. A confession at the foot of a pagan shrine, the harshest rebuke six verses later, and glory on a mountain a week after that.

93513.title: The Galilean Ministry of Jesus Explained (5 of 12)
93513.excerpt: The busiest year of the ministry, opening with a sermon that got him thrown off a cliff. Capernaum, the Twelve, the parables, and the crowd that walked away.

93512.title: The Early Judean Ministry of Jesus (4 of 12)
93512.excerpt: The year the Synoptic Gospels skip entirely. Cana, the first temple cleansing, Nicodemus at night, and the woman at the well, all recorded only by John.

93511.title: Why Was Jesus Baptized and Tempted? (3 of 12)
93511.excerpt: John baptized for repentance, which raises a problem when Jesus steps into the water. What the baptism accomplished and why the testing runs forty days.

93510.title: What Did Jesus Do Before He Was 30? (2 of 12)
93510.excerpt: The Gospels give one scene between infancy and baptism. What the silence covers, what a tekton actually was, and why the apocryphal filling-in is refused.

93508.title: When Was Jesus Born? The Nativity Explained (1 of 12)
93508.excerpt: Not year zero, not December, and probably not a stable. What Luke and Matthew actually record about the birth, and where the familiar picture came from.

93584.title: How Is Luke Structured? The Journey to Jerusalem (1 of 1)
93584.excerpt: A third of Luke is a journey that could have been summarised in a verse. Why the travel narrative exists, and what the Gospel does that the others do not.

93585.title: The Genealogy and Joseph the Just Man (1 of 4)
93585.excerpt: Four women appear in a list that should have had none, and every one of the choices is pointed. Then Joseph decides what justice means and a woman lives.

93744.title: How Did the Apostle Paul Die? (8 of 12)
93744.excerpt: Scripture never narrates it. What the earliest sources say about Rome, Nero, and the sword, which details are late, and whether he ever reached Spain.

93737.title: Paul’s Shipwreck and Voyage to Rome (7 of 12)
93737.excerpt: Fourteen days driven before a storm, 276 people saved, and a snake on Malta. Then two years under guard in Rome, where Acts stops mid-sentence on purpose.

93733.title: Why Was Paul Arrested in Jerusalem? (6 of 12)
93733.excerpt: A false rumour started a riot, Roman soldiers pulled him out of a lynching, and two years of custody followed. The arrest that carried him to Caesar in Rome.

93727.title: Paul’s Third Journey: 3 Years in Ephesus (5 of 12)
93727.excerpt: His longest stay anywhere, in the occult capital of Asia, ending in a riot by silversmiths whose trade was collapsing. Plus the letters written along the way.

93726.title: Paul’s Second Missionary Journey Explained (4 of 12)
93726.excerpt: A quarrel, a vision, and the gospel crossing into Europe. Philippi, Athens, Corinth, and the inscription that anchors the whole chronology of Paul’s life.

93725.title: Paul’s First Missionary Journey and Acts 15 (3 of 12)
93725.excerpt: Cyprus, Galatia, a stoning, and then the meeting that decided whether Gentile converts had to become Jews. The journey that forced the Jerusalem Council.

93684.title: The Damascus Road and Paul’s Hidden Years (2 of 12)
93684.excerpt: Acts tells the Damascus story three times, then skips roughly a decade in a verse. What happened on the road, and what happened during the years nobody records.

93683.title: Who Was Saul of Tarsus Before Damascus? (1 of 12)
93683.excerpt: A Hebrew of Hebrews, a Greek-speaking citizen of a university city, and a Roman citizen from birth. Three worlds in one man, and he used all three later.

93760.title: Who Was Polycrates of Ephesus? (8 of 9)
93760.excerpt: A letter about the date of Easter, written to defend Asian custom against Rome, is where the claim that Philip is buried at Hierapolis comes from. What it says.

93759.title: Who Was Hegesippus and What Did He Record? (7 of 9)
93759.excerpt: The fullest account of how James the brother of Jesus died comes from a lost second-century book. What Hegesippus wrote, and how much of it can be trusted.

93756.title: How Reliable Is Irenaeus as a Source? (4 of 9)
93756.excerpt: He heard Polycarp, who knew the apostles, which makes him our shortest chain to the first century. He also thought Jesus lived to nearly fifty. Both are true.

93755.title: Who Was Clement of Rome? 1 Clement (3 of 9)
93755.excerpt: A letter from Rome to Corinth around AD 95, and the earliest outside notice of Peter and Paul. What 1 Clement says, and what it deliberately does not say.

93473.title: How Do We Know What Happened to the Apostles? (1 of 9)
93473.excerpt: Almost everything we know about the church after Acts comes from a handful of men, and most of their books are lost. Who the witnesses are and how far they go.

93787.title: Jesus and Women: What Had Changed by His Day (4 of 4)
93787.excerpt: Ruth, Esther, Deborah and Judith were heroines in the older literature. By the first century the position had moved, and the movement is well documented.

93776.title: The Woman at the Well and the Man With No Bucket (3 of 4)
93776.excerpt: He sits on the wellhead with no means of drawing water and opens by asking her for help. The longest conversation in the Gospels starts from a position of need.

93762.title: The Woman Caught in Adultery: Where Was the Man? (1 of 4)
93762.excerpt: The law they cite requires both parties, and they brought one. What the accusers were actually doing, and why the manuscript question does not settle it.

93682.title: The Parable of the Weeds and Why God Waits (26 of 26)
93682.excerpt: The servants want to clear the field and the farmer stops them. Wright on why the weeds are inside Israel, and whether the church may ever do the weeding.

93681.title: The Hidden Treasure and the Pearl of Great Price (25 of 26)
93681.excerpt: The man hides what he found and buys the field without telling the owner, which is not obviously honest. Why the awkwardness is worth facing rather than fixing.

93680.title: The Mustard Seed and the Yeast Explained (24 of 26)
93680.excerpt: A mustard bush is not the cedar Ezekiel promised, and yeast is an image of corruption everywhere else. Both parables pick the wrong thing deliberately.

93679.title: The Parable of the Sower and the Four Soils (23 of 26)
93679.excerpt: The one parable Jesus explains. What the soils mean, Wright’s reading of it as Israel’s return from exile, and three answers to why he quotes Isaiah 6.

93678.title: The Good Shepherd: A Claim to Be King (22 of 26)
93678.excerpt: Shepherd language in the Bible is royal language, so this is not a picture of gentleness. It is a claim to the throne, made against named rival claimants.

93677.title: The Unforgiving Servant and the Impossible Debt (21 of 26)
93677.excerpt: Ten thousand talents was not a large debt, it was an unpayable one, and the second debt is real money. The gap between the two numbers is the parable.

93676.title: The Sheep and the Goats: Who Are the Brothers? (20 of 26)
93676.excerpt: Everything turns on the phrase the least of these my brothers, which Matthew has already defined elsewhere. That changes who is judged and on what basis.

93675.title: The Prodigal Son: What the Village Was Waiting For (19 of 26)
93675.excerpt: The father runs to reach his son before the village does. A ceremony was waiting for a man who lost family land among Gentiles, and the embrace prevents it.

93674.title: The Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin Explained (18 of 26)
93674.excerpt: Three parables in Luke 15 answer one complaint about eating with sinners, and reading them as separate lessons loses the argument they build together.

93672.title: The Ten Bridesmaids: Why They Would Not Share (16 of 26)
93672.excerpt: The wise refuse to share their oil, which cuts against everything else Jesus taught. What the oil actually stands for, and why it could never be lent.

93671.title: The Parable of the Pounds and the Hated King (15 of 26)
93671.excerpt: Luke’s version is not the Talents with different numbers. A delegation opposes the king, and the first hearers knew exactly which delegation that was.

93670.title: The Tenants in the Vineyard: Squatters Rights (14 of 26)
93670.excerpt: The tenants murder the heir hoping to gain the estate, which sounds insane until you know what they were counting on. Why the owner sends his son alone.

93669.title: The Workers in the Vineyard: A Fair Wage? (13 of 26)
93669.excerpt: The owner keeps going back to the market himself, in the heat, when he could send a manager. That detail is the parable, and it changes the complaint.

93662.title: The Two Builders: Why the Storm Hits Both (10 of 26)
93662.excerpt: Both houses take the same storm, which rules out the reading most people carry. What digging down to rock actually involved and what the foundation is.

93652.title: The Good Samaritan: What the Parable Answers (9 of 26)
93652.excerpt: The lawyer asks who his neighbour is and never gets an answer, because the question itself was wrong. What the priest was actually weighing on that road.

93640.title: Lazarus and the Rich Man: What It Teaches (8 of 26)
93640.excerpt: The parable used to build a map of the afterlife is not answering that question. What it is answering, and why the rich man never stops giving orders.

93626.title: The Parable of the Great Banquet Explained (7 of 26)
93626.excerpt: Bailey reads the three excuses as a public insult; most commentators hear lame excuses. Why the guest list, not the excuses, answers a seven-hundred-year argument.

93623.title: The Parable of the Rich Fool Explained (6 of 26)
93623.excerpt: Jesus refuses to answer a request for justice, which is startling until you see what he thought the request was a symptom of. Why he treats it as illness.

93622.title: The Parable of the Unjust Steward Explained (5 of 26)
93622.excerpt: The hardest parable in the Gospels. A manager cheats his employer and gets praised for it, and Bailey’s reading turns on a detail most translations bury.

93621.title: The Wedding Feast and the Man Without a Garment (4 of 26)
93621.excerpt: A man is dragged in off the street and then thrown out for what he is wearing. Why the ending is not arbitrary, and what the parable is actually answering.

93620.title: The Pharisee and the Tax Collector Explained (3 of 26)
93620.excerpt: The tax collector does not ask for mercy in the vague sense. He asks for atonement, and the temple sacrifice is burning behind him at the moment he says it.

93614.title: The Parable of the Talents Explained (2 of 26)
93614.excerpt: The third servant was not being prudent, and the master never confirms the charge against him. Why this parable is hard, and what Bailey, Wright and Snodgrass make of the hard parts.

93611.title: The Parables of Jesus: Complete List and Guide (1 of 26)
93611.excerpt: Most teaching treats a parable as a container: find the point, take it out, throw the story away. Kenneth Bailey argues the mechanism runs the other way, and that a parable is closer to a house you are invited to move into. That is what this series runs on, and the index of all twenty-six posts is further down.

93610.title: Who Was Dagon? From Philistia to Lovecraft (15 of 15)
93610.excerpt: He was not a fish god, or at least nobody can show it. Who Dagon actually was, what happened in his temple, and how one guess became the version we know.

93609.title: What Happened After the Exile? Ezra to Malachi (14 of 15)
93609.excerpt: A smaller temple, a rebuilt wall, and the last prophet before four centuries of silence. What the returning exiles built and what they were still waiting for.

93608.title: What Was the Babylonian Exile? (13 of 15)
93608.excerpt: Seventy years without a temple, a land, or a king, and the period that made Judaism what it became. Daniel, Ezekiel, Esther, and the decree that ended it.

93607.title: What Is the Book of Jonah Really About? (12 of 15)
93607.excerpt: Not the fish. A prophet who succeeds completely and is furious about it, and a book ending on a question aimed at the reader rather than at the prophet.

93606.title: How Did Judah Fall to Babylon? (11 of 15)
93606.excerpt: Judah outlived the north by 136 years, produced a great reform, and fell anyway. The prophets who warned, the three deportations, and the temple burned.

93605.title: Why Did Israel Split Into Two Kingdoms? (10 of 15)
93605.excerpt: One bad answer about taxes split the nation permanently. The northern kingdom, the prophets God kept sending to it, and the Assyrian deportation that ended it.

93604.title: What Are the Wisdom Books of the Bible? (9 of 15)
93604.excerpt: Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Song of Solomon. Four books that argue with each other, and the canon keeps all four without resolving the tension.

93603.title: Saul, David, and Solomon: The United Kingdom (8 of 15)
93603.excerpt: Israel asks for a king and gets exactly what it asked for. Three reigns, one eternal covenant, and a kingdom that splits the very moment Solomon has died.

93596.title: What Was the Period of the Judges? (7 of 15)
93596.excerpt: A repeating cycle of collapse and rescue, deliverers who get steadily worse as the book goes on, and a closing line that diagnoses the entire era honestly.

93592.title: How Did Israel Conquer Canaan? (6 of 15)
93592.excerpt: Jericho, Ai, and the campaigns, plus the hardest question in the Old Testament. What the conquest accounts say and how the difficulty is usually handled.

93591.title: What Happened in the Wilderness Wanderings? (5 of 15)
93591.excerpt: The tabernacle, the golden calf, and a forty-year sentence handed down for one refusal at the border. What the wilderness years cost and what they were for.

93590.title: What Was the Exodus from Egypt? (4 of 15)
93590.excerpt: The plagues were aimed at specific gods, the Passover was instituted before the deliverance, and Sinai turned a rescued mob into a nation under covenant.

93589.title: What Is the Book of Job About? (3 of 15)
93589.excerpt: It opens in a heavenly council Job never learns about, and God’s answer never mentions the reason. Why the book refuses the question it seems to be asking.

93588.title: Who Were the Patriarchs? Abraham to Joseph (2 of 15)
93588.excerpt: Four generations, one promise, and a family that keeps nearly wrecking it. What the covenant with Abraham actually said and how it survived down to Egypt.

93587.title: What Happens in Genesis 1-11? (1 of 15)
93587.excerpt: Creation, the fall, the flood, and Babel. Three rebellions rather than one, and the third explains why the rest of the Old Testament looks the way it does.

93024.title: What Raiders of the Lost Ark Got Right About the Ark of the Covenant
93024.excerpt: Indiana Jones and the Nazis both believed the same thing about the Ark of the Covenant: whoever holds it holds the power. 1 Samuel 4-6 is the block of chapters written to take that idea apart. Here is what the movie got right, what it inverted, and what would actually have happened in that canyon.

93027.title: Where Is the Ark of the Covenant?
93027.excerpt: Raiders of the Lost Ark ends with the Ark crated up in a government warehouse, and every tradition has its own warehouse. Here is every serious claim about where the Ark is today, ranked by what actually backs it, and the verse in Jeremiah that nobody quotes because it tells you to stop looking.

93377.title: Reversing Hermon: The Watchers and the Mission of Jesus
93377.excerpt: Genesis 6 gets hurried past. The New Testament writers did not hurry past it. A chapter-by-chapter guide to Heiser’s Reversing Hermon and the Book of Enoch underneath it.

93011.title: The Names I Didn’t Know
93011.excerpt: I started with a simple question: how did the Bible on my desk get here? The material wasn’t too hard. It was full of people I had never heard of, mentioned as if I already knew them. Chasing those names down turned out to be the whole method.

93008.title: Jerome: The Man Who Went Back to the Hebrew
93008.excerpt: He learned Hebrew in a desert in his thirties, when almost nobody in the Latin West bothered with it, and then spent thirty-four years translating the Old Testament from the original. The Bible on your desk still carries the shape of that decision, and so does the most famous mistranslation ever pinned on anyone.

92861.title: The King in Yellow — The Borrowed Ruler (3 of 4)
92861.excerpt: The fraud voice runs the same play every time. It redefines the word until my method falls outside the definition, then convicts me for being outside a line it just drew. The ruler I inherited without knowing, and why the church I walk into rarely has a seat for what I’m built to do. Section 3 of 4 in The King in Yellow series.

92936.title: The Book of the Watchers: 1 Enoch 1–36, Read Aloud
92936.excerpt: 1 Enoch chapters one through thirty-six, the Book of the Watchers, in the R. H. Charles 1917 translation. Not a summary and not commentary, just the book itself, formatted to be listened to straight through in five movements.

92925.title: Which Book of Enoch? 1, 2, 3 Enoch, Jubilees, and Why None of Them Made the Cut
92925.excerpt: Someone hands you “the Book of Enoch” like it’s a lost chapter of Scripture. There is no single Book of Enoch. There are at least four Enoch-branded works, written centuries apart, in three languages, and Josephus already told the Romans why none of them counted.

92910.title: The Gate That Was Never There
92910.excerpt: You have heard the sermon: a low postern gate in Jerusalem’s wall called the Eye of the Needle, where a camel could squeeze through if you unloaded it and got it on its knees. There was no such gate. The claim shows up a thousand years after Jesus said the words, and tracing it turned out to be more interesting than debunking it.

92836.title: What the Image of God Actually Is, and What It Means to Be an Imager
92836.excerpt: Ask most people what the image of God is and you’ll hear the same answer: our reason, our conscience, the divine spark inside us. It sounds right, and it does not survive contact with the text. What replaces it is bigger, stranger, and far more useful.

92771.title: The Drive Home From Mead
92771.excerpt: I smoked heavy for ten years. Then one afternoon, driving home from the paper mill, I ran out, and the thing that had owned me for a decade just let go. Here’s what I think actually happened, and why it has almost nothing to do with willpower.

90326.title: You Are the Project
90326.excerpt: Epictetus was a slave. When he says focus on what’s in your power, he speaks from the widest gap there is between control and circumstance. You are the project. But, Paul adds, not the only one working on it.

90325.title: What Makes a Happy Life
90325.excerpt: Marcus had everything Rome could give and warned himself, in private, that none of it was what makes a life. Most of what we call needs is scaffolding we’ve mistaken for the building, and the things we claim not to want are often just things we won’t pay for yet.

90314.title: Washing Away the Dust of Life
90314.excerpt: Marcus Aurelius prescribes looking up at the stars to settle the dust of ordinary frustration. Not escapism but calibration: a deliberate reset of scale that puts the thing back in its real size. The Psalms make the same move.

90313.title: Very Little Is Needed
90313.excerpt: In Philippians 4:11, Paul borrows the Stoic word autarkēs but adds one word that changes everything: he had to learn it. The contentment he means is formed only by the circumstances most of us spend our lives avoiding.

90312.title: The Ten Plagues of Egypt
90312.excerpt: The plagues weren’t weather events or just political pressure. Heiser reads Exodus 7-12 as a divine-council confrontation, with Yahweh dismantling the religious order of Egypt and exposing its gods as powerless, judgment building toward the final Passover night.

90308.title: The Mind Is Its Own Place
90308.excerpt: Milton put the line in Satan’s mouth as a warning. Marcus made the hopeful version. Paul calls it taking every thought captive. The mind is where your actual power lives, and the discipline is showing up to fight on it.

90296.title: Reset
90296.excerpt: 2,600 days of closed Apple Watch rings. The discipline that actually mattered was never the streak. It was the restart. Building the muscle that refuses to let one missed day write the story that ends the whole thing.

90292.title: No Harm, No Foul
90292.excerpt: Marcus Aurelius on harm as a judgment we assign, not a fact we receive, and the honest line between naming a real injury and reflexively turning every setback into a wound. Paul works the same ground from Romans 8.

90291.title: Moses at the Threshold: The Circumcision Crisis
90291.excerpt: Exodus 4:24-26 is one of the strangest passages in the Torah. Yahweh attacks Moses on the road to Egypt, and Zipporah stops it with a flint knife and a covenant act. A divine council reading of why the household had to come first, and where the Hebrew refuses to settle.

90290.title: Lesser Gods of the Old Testament: Pagan Deities
90290.excerpt: The Old Testament names dozens of rival gods: Baal, Asherah, Molech, Dagon, the Queen of Heaven, the host of heaven. A working reference to who they were and what each one claimed authority over, read through the Divine Council framework.

90288.title: Jephthah’s Study of Judges 11
90288.excerpt: Did Jephthah sacrifice his daughter or dedicate her to lifelong service? A full read of Judges 11: the outcast warrior, the rash vow, and the silence of God, working through Wilcock and Block on what the text actually says.

90301.title: The Tool Takes the Shape of the Hand
90301.excerpt: Socrates refused to write because he feared writing would let us stop remembering. Plato wrote anyway. We barely know Socrates because of it. The same argument is happening again with AI.

91499.title: Divine Council Inventory: Heavenly Beings and Fallen Entities
91499.excerpt: The Old Testament presents a populated heavenly realm: beings of various ranks, roles, and alignments operating within Yahweh’s cosmic order. In Heiser’s divine council framework, these are real entities with assigned functions, some faithful, some in rebellion.

90322.title: What Is a King? Will You Bow Now? (6 of 6)
90322.excerpt: Five sections of preparation, one question. We are between the two stages right now. The cross is past. The conquering King is future. The position you take now is the position you keep.

90289.title: Judges 17–18: Micah, Dan, and the Idol
90289.excerpt: Idolatry in Judges 17-18 starts in one man’s house with stolen silver, moves into the priesthood when a Levite takes a paycheck, and ends with a whole tribe running a rival shrine at Dan. A study of the appendix to Judges, read with Block and the divine council framework.

90321.title: What Is a King? The Witness and the Unveiling (5 of 6)
90321.excerpt: You are responsible for the witness. You are not responsible for the unveiling. The weight modern American Christianity transfers onto the witness was never Scripture’s to give.

90286.title: Don’t Get Lost in Other People’s Minds
90286.excerpt: Marcus catches something most self-help spends hundreds of pages circling: we say we love ourselves but spend our energy managing what other people think of us.

90320.title: What Is a King? The Counterfeit King (4 of 6)
90320.excerpt: The serpent does not need to convince you the gospel is false. That is too obvious. What he can do is fake the recognition just well enough that you bow to something that looks almost right.

90268.title: The Chosen: Biblical vs. Fictional Characters
90268.excerpt: The Chosen has reached more people with the biblical narrative than most films in a generation. A working inventory of which characters come from Scripture and which were invented for the screen.

90319.title: What Is a King? The Return of the King (3 of 6)
90319.excerpt: The imago Dei still knows what kingship looks like, even after the world has stripped every reference for it from daily life. There is one scene in cinema that proves it every time.

90318.title: What Is a King? Slave to Christ (2 of 6)
90318.excerpt: Paul opens Romans with a self-description 2026 American ears cannot hear correctly. Doulos Christou, slave of Christ. The softening costs more than translators know.

90324.title: What Is a King? The Room Defines the King (1 of 6)
90324.excerpt: Kingliness is not generated by the king. It is generated by the room. The bowing, the lowered eyes, the held breath, the way bodies rearrange in space. A 2026 American has nothing to fill the word with, and that is the problem.

90269.title: ABBA, Father
90269.excerpt: You have probably heard a sermon claim that Abba means “Daddy.” That idea traces back largely to Joachim Jeremias in the mid-twentieth century, and it has stuck in popular preaching ever since. But the case does not hold up, and what the word actually means is something heavier.
